decontamination_notes: Real routing denial-of-service fix from pallets/werkzeug PR #3238 ('int URL 404s when longer than max_int_str_digits', https://github.com/pallets/werkzeug/pull/3238), merged 2026-08-13 -- after the training cutoffs of the models evaluated here (e.g. Opus 5, May 2026), so the specific fix is not in their training data (decontaminated: true), with upstream_merged recorded as proof. The URL routing `<int:...>` converter calls int() on the matched path segment. Python caps int()-from-string at ~4300 digits (the CVE-2020-10735 mitigation) and raises ValueError beyond that; the converter did not catch it, so a request URL with a very long digit run made routing raise an unhandled ValueError (a 500 / crash) instead of simply not matching the route -- a DoS from a single request. The fix catches the ValueError in NumberConverter.to_python (routing/converters.py) and raises ValidationError, and matcher.py chains it to a non-match, so the request cleanly 404s. werkzeug is pure Python; its package __init__ imports MarkupSafe, so MarkupSafe is vendored into repo/_vendor (built for the sandbox's linux-amd64) and hidden tests run offline with PYTHONPATH=src:_vendor on the base image (Python 3.12, default int-str-digits limit 4300). Repo sliced at the PR base commit (21.9k LOC; converter without the guard); BSD-3-Clause LICENSE preserved. Coverage floor: 3 fail_to_pass (a 5000-, 10000-, and 4301-digit int URL each raise an uncaught ValueError at base and cleanly 404 after the fix) plus a 2-check regression guard (a normal integer still matches and converts; an integer within the digit limit still matches).
